title: Client snapshot handshake and orphaned stream archival for partial-generation cleanup
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Observed customer impact when clients disconnect mid-generation: memory pressure on router pods from retained in-flight state, bursty retey attempts causing repeated partial outputs, and inconsistent resume behavior across SDKs and compatibility layers. Current mechanisms (basic resume tokens + TTL sweep) are insufficient for long-lived disconnected sessions and for workloads with heavy tool-calling/structured-output where partial results are sensitive. This ticket defines a client snapshot handshake and an orphaned-stream archival flow to safely reclaim resources and enable deterministic resumes or tombstoning when resumption is impossible.
proposal: 1) Introduce a short-lived client snapshot handshake: when a client opens a streaming session, the server issues an epoched snapshot token that encodes minimal session checkpoints (sequence id, KV cache digest, last function call state, and epoch). 2) On graceful disconnect, client uploads a compact final snapshot; on abrupt disconnect, server attempts automated snapshotting at safe cut points (token boundary or function-call boundary). 3) Implement an orphaned-stream archival pipeline that serializes compact partial generation manifests to blobstore with tiered TTLs (fast reclaim for non-resumable sessions, extended retention for sessions flagged resumable). 4) Add a deterministic tombstone protocol: after retention TTL, stream is marked tombstoned and resume attempts receive a clear error with guidance and stored partial output links (for debugging/forensics). 5) Expose compatibility-layer hooks: SDKs receive standardized resume/abort codes and an explicit client-driven snapshot API to opt-in for longer retention.
tradeoffs: Increased implementation complexity in routing and session lifecycle code vs. improved resource reclamation and clearer resume semantics.
Storing compact manifests in blobstore increases operational storage costs; mitigated by tiered TTL and size caps per session.
Automated server-side snapshotting may capture partial function-call state that SDKs can't fully interpret; we will restrict automated snapshots to function-call-safe boundaries.
Adding epoched tokens requires careful key rotation and validation to avoid resume incompatibilities across runtime upgrades.
Short TTLs risk breaking legitimate long-pause resumption; provide an opt-in extended retention flag for enterprise tenants with Dedicated/Private deployments.
plan: Design token format (epoch, sequence, KV-digest, function-call-checksum) and document compatibility guarantees
Implement snapshot handshake in router: token issuance, validation, and compact manifest serialization
Build archival writer to blobstore with size enforcement and TTL tiers; integrate with existing retention tooling
Server-side graceful/abrupt disconnect handling: trigger snapshot attempt, fall back to manifest-only archival if runtime constraints apply
Add resume API endpoints that accept snapshot tokens and either replay KV cache or return clear tombstone errors
SDK changes: add snapshot API, resume helpers, and mapping of new server error codes to developer-facing messages
End-to-end tests: chaotic disconnects, function-call boundary cases, cross-version resume, storage TTL expiry
Run canary on runtime-1.20 for low-traffic customers and monitor memory pressure, resume success rate, and storage usage
acceptance_criteria: Router memory usage from disconnected sessions reduces by >= 75% for a 1-hour disconnect workload in canary compared to baseline
Resume success rate for eligible sessions >= 98% in synthetic tests covering function-call and structured-output flows
Tombstone path returns deterministic error code with link to stored partial manifest for forensic analysis
SDKs map new server error codes into documented user-facing messages and provide an example for rehydration flow
Blobstore storage increase attributable to manifests remains within projected budget for the canary cohort

2026-03-04 - QA: Found a race when client resumes while archival write is still pending; adding short blocking window in resume path to wait for manifest finalization (up to 500ms).
